subject: Post-call recap: Stellar Supply bakeoff framing & next steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Richards <ava@stellarsupply.com>, Brian Cole <brian@stellarsupply.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-10T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Stellar Supply bakeoff framing & next steps

Hi Ava / Brian —

Thanks again for a great conversation today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned. I pasted the technical follow-ups below for Marcus.

Key pain points you confirmed
- Bursty order-load spikes (Q4 peak usage) causing slow-downs in downstream services when inference latency exceeds 250ms.
- High per-token cost on your current stack (concern for margin-sensitive B2B customers).
- Need for predictable tail latency (p95/p99) and strong observability for auditing.

Goals you described
- Stay under 200ms p95 for the majority of inference calls; p99 SLA targets to be defined during bakeoff.
- Reduce inference unit cost by ~30% vs current baseline.
- Private VPC option for sensitive customer flows and audit logs retention for 12 months.

Competitive context you mentioned
- You previously evaluated Nimbus (good throughput, opaque runtimes) and VertexCloud (tight integration with cloud infra but costly ops). You asked how Redwood would behave differently across load spikes and in a constrained-budget scenario.

Proposed bakeoff scope (high level)
1) Latency tests: p50/p95/p99 under steady-state and spike patterns (we'll provide harness).
2) Cost simulation: token-level accounting for the test window and projected Q4 monthly run-rate.
3) Degradation plan: configured fallbacks to smaller quantized variants and cold-start behavior.
4) Security: VPC deployment checklist + SOC2 artifact list (we'll attach evidence).

Immediate asks / commitments
- From you: confirm target SLA for p99 and whether 12-month audit log retention is a hard requirement.
- From us (action items below): we will ship a bakeoff brief, a lightweight test harness, and a proposed schedule for a 1-week comparative run.

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-brief.pdf (bakeoff plan), stellarsupply-answers.xlsx (notes from today's call).

Proposed schedule
- Aug 17: kick-off alignment call (30m) — who should join from your infra team?
- Aug 18–21: test window (we'll run parallel scenarios)
- Aug 24: readout and recommended config / pricing model

If that captures it, we'll send the formal bakeoff plan and a calendar invite for Aug 17.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

Thanks Kimberly — this is great, appreciate the clear summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- p99 SLA: we'd like to target 300ms initially, then tighten to 200ms based on bakeoff results.
- Audit logs: 12 months is ideal but we can accept shorter if there are cost tradeoffs; please surface options.
- Team for kick-off: I'll be on the call, and I'll invite our infra lead (tech@stellarsupply.com) and our procurement partner (brian@stellarsupply.com).

Please include any security artifacts you can share ahead of the kick-off — the procurement team will want them.

-Ava
Director of Product, Stellar Supply

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Stellar Supply bakeoff framing & next steps (tech plan)

Thanks — adding the technical plan from our side so the group can review before the kick-off. High level test harness and responsibilities below.

Test plan (detailed)
- Harness: lightweight Gatling-based driver + a token accounting wrapper we supply. Will simulate both steady-state (20 RPS) and spike (400 RPS for 5 min) patterns.
- Models: we'll run three variants — full FP16 model (baseline), 4-bit quantized variant, and a distilled low-latency variant. We will also include our cold-start bucket and a warmed cache run.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, tail-latency latency buckets, throughput, per-token CPU/GPU time, memory/KV cache hit rate, and end-to-end cost estimates.
- Environment: Hosted mode (our hosted infra) and a dedicated VPC run if you can provide a test subnet (optional for bakeoff, required for security audit).

Open questions for Stellar Supply
1) Can your infra team provide a test subnet (short-lived) for a VPC run, or should we keep the initial run to hosted only?
2) Do you have sample traffic logs (anonymized) we can use to shape the spike pattern, or should we use our standard ecommerce spike profile?

Timeline & owners
- Aug 12: deliver test harness + runbook (Marcus)
- Aug 17: kick-off call (Kimberly + Marcus + Stellar infra)
- Aug 18–21: test execution (Marcus + Stellar infra)
- Aug 24: readout (Kimberly + Marcus)

I'll attach a minimal runbook and the driver link in the drive folder referenced in the bakeoff brief.

—Marcus
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
